rows.text: At its meeting on 26 February 2007, the Monetary Council considered the latest economic and financial developments and voted to leave the central bank base rate unchanged at 8.00%.
At its meeting on 26 February 2007, the Monetary Council considered the latest economic and financial developments and voted to leave the central bank base rate unchanged at 8.00%.

In the February update of the Quarterly Report on Inflation, the central projection conditional on staff’s assumptions is for inflation to fall significantly from 2007 H2, following the high outturns for CPI in the next few months.

In the Monetary Council’s judgement, inflation may slow significantly within the period relevant for monetary policy, i.e. in 2008, as a result of very subdued domestic demand and loose labour market conditions.
